groups.title: Foundations & Logic
groups.description: Proofs, logic, set theory, computability and model theory

groups.title: Algebra
groups.description: Linear, abstract, commutative and homological algebra; categories, representations and algebraic geometry

groups.title: Analysis
groups.description: Calculus, real and complex analysis, measure, functional analysis, Fourier analysis and differential equations

groups.title: Geometry & Topology
groups.description: Point-set and algebraic topology, differential geometry, homotopy and symplectic geometry

groups.title: Number Theory
groups.description: Elementary, algebraic and analytic number theory; class field theory, modular forms and arithmetic geometry

groups.title: Discrete Mathematics
groups.description: Combinatorics, graphs, enumeration and generating functions

groups.title: Probability & Dynamics
groups.description: Undergraduate and measure-theoretic probability, dynamical systems and ergodic theory

books.title: Book of Proof
books.author: Richard Hammack
books.note: A transition from calculation to proofs, with sets, induction and cardinality. Selected solutions help self-study; it is preparation rather than an advanced subject text.

books.title: forall x: Calgary
books.author: P. D. Magnus, Tim Button, Aaron Thomas-Bolduc and Richard Zach, with contributors
books.note: Introduces formal languages, truth tables and natural deduction. Exercises and solutions support a first logic course; metatheory is developed further in the next text.
books.label: Full HTML & PDF

books.title: Sets, Logic, Computation
books.author: Richard Zach
books.note: Develops completeness, compactness and undecidability after elementary formal logic. A structured bridge from proof systems to mathematical metatheory.
books.label: Full book & PDF

books.title: Incompleteness and Computability
books.author: Richard Zach
books.note: Covers recursive functions, arithmetization and Gödel's theorems. Best read after a first metalogic course, not as an introduction to proofs.
books.label: Full book & PDF

books.title: Set Theory: An Open Introduction
books.author: Tim Button
books.note: Explains the set-theoretic foundations of mathematics and the motivation for ZFC. Its emphasis is conceptual and philosophical, not graduate forcing theory.
books.label: Full book & PDF

books.title: Lecture Notes — Model Theory (Math 411)
books.author: Anand Pillay
books.note: A concise graduate treatment beginning with structures and languages. The lecture-note format rewards familiarity with logical notation and independent proof work.

books.title: Linear Algebra
books.author: Jim Hefferon
books.note: Balances Gaussian elimination with vector spaces and proofs. Worked solutions to all exercises are useful for independent study; suitable before an operator-focused second course.
books.label: Full book & solutions

books.title: Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th edition
books.author: Sheldon Axler
books.note: A proof-based, operator-centered second course that introduces determinants late. Especially useful for structural understanding; not designed primarily as a computational matrix handbook.

books.title: Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications
books.author: Thomas W. Judson
books.note: Groups, rings and fields are accompanied by applications and exercises. Reviewers note broad undergraduate coverage; a useful first algebra text rather than a graduate reference.
books.label: Read full HTML

books.title: Group Theory
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: A compact graduate introduction, including finite-group representations. Concise exposition makes prior exposure to algebra helpful.

books.title: Fields and Galois Theory
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: Develops field extensions, Galois theory and transcendence degree. A focused continuation after groups, rings and basic fields.

books.title: A Primer of Commutative Algebra
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: A concise foundation for algebraic geometry and number theory, covering localization, integrality, dimension and completion. 'Introductory' here presupposes substantial algebra.

books.title: A Term of Commutative Algebra
books.author: Allen Altman and Steven Kleiman
books.note: A course-sized development with exercises and solutions. Suitable for systematic study after abstract algebra; its ring-and-module language is more demanding than a first algebra course.
books.label: Full PDF via MIT

books.title: Notes on Basic Homological Algebra
books.author: Andrew Baker
books.note: A compact entry into homological methods for readers already comfortable with modules. Useful as course notes; less expansive than a comprehensive graduate textbook.

books.title: The Stacks Project — Homological Algebra
books.author: The Stacks Project Authors
books.note: A detailed searchable reference with stable theorem tags. Use the Homology, Derived Categories and related chapters; it is not a gentle sequential first course.
books.label: Read full reference

books.title: Category Theory in Context
books.author: Emily Riehl
books.note: Explains universal properties, Yoneda, adjunctions and Kan extensions through mathematical examples. Algebra and topology greatly improve accessibility despite minimal formal prerequisites.

books.title: Elements of ∞-Category Theory
books.author: Emily Riehl and Dominic Verity
books.note: A substantial treatment of higher categories for mathematically mature readers. A later step after ordinary category theory, not a shortcut around its foundations.

books.title: Introduction to Representation Theory
books.author: Pavel Etingof et al.
books.note: Introduces representations using algebra and many exercises. Appropriate for strong undergraduates with linear algebra; the pace assumes comfort with abstract structures.
books.prerequisites: Linear algebra; groups, rings and fields.

books.title: Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
books.author: Pavel Etingof
books.note: A graduate course connecting Lie groups, Lie algebras and representations. Initial manifold material helps orientation but does not remove the need for mathematical maturity.
books.prerequisites: Abstract algebra; topology and smooth manifolds.

books.title: Tensor Categories
books.author: Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki, Dmitri Nikshych and Victor Ostrik
books.note: Develops the categorical setting for representation theory. A specialist continuation rather than an introductory algebra text; link to the authorized author-hosted edition.
books.label: Full book via author's page

books.title: Algebraic Geometry
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: A first graduate course centered on abstract algebraic varieties, providing a bridge toward schemes.
books.prerequisites: Fields, Galois theory and commutative algebra.

books.title: The Rising Sea: Foundations of Algebraic Geometry
books.author: Ravi Vakil
books.note: A broad, exercise-rich development of schemes and their geometry. The October 21, 2025 author edition closely matches the published text; substantial algebra is essential.
books.archiveNote: July 27, 2024 archive · CC BY-NC-ND 3.0; unchanged noncommercial copy.

books.title: The Stacks Project
books.author: The Stacks Project Authors
books.note: An extensive open reference on schemes and related algebra. Stable tags are useful for precise citations; selective consultation is more practical than cover-to-cover reading.
books.label: Read full reference

books.title: Calculus, Volume 1
books.author: Gilbert Strang and Edwin 'Jed' Herman
books.note: An illustrated first course with examples and applications. Useful for computational foundations; a proof-based real analysis text is needed for a mathematics-major transition.

books.title: Basic Analysis I
books.author: Jiří Lebl
books.note: Builds real-line analysis before metric spaces, with many exercises. Reviewers describe it as adaptable to undergraduate courses; self-study requires actively writing proofs.

books.title: Basic Analysis II
books.author: Jiří Lebl
books.note: Continues to multivariable analysis, inverse and implicit function theorems, approximation and Fourier series. A natural sequel, not a replacement for measure theory.

books.title: Measure, Integration & Real Analysis
books.author: Sheldon Axler
books.note: A graduate treatment of measure and integration with connections to functional analysis and Fourier analysis. Suitable after proof-based analysis, not elementary calculus.

books.title: Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis: Working the Complex Field
books.author: Jiří Lebl
books.note: A first graduate course from holomorphic functions to conformal mapping and analytic continuation. Appendices review analysis prerequisites; exercises remain important for understanding.
books.prerequisites: Real analysis; metric spaces; multivariable calculus.

books.title: Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
books.author: Jiří Lebl
books.note: A course-length tour of pseudoconvexity, CR geometry and the ∂̄-problem. Broad exposure rather than an exhaustive reference, with exercises used throughout.

books.title: Introduction to Functional Analysis (18.102)
books.author: Richard Melrose
books.note: A course-length development of Banach spaces, Lebesgue integration, Hilbert spaces and applications. The author notes ongoing revisions; useful before more specialized graduate functional analysis.
books.prerequisites: Proof-based real analysis; metric spaces; linear algebra.

books.title: The Fourier Transform and its Applications
books.author: Brad Osgood
books.note: An example-driven introduction from Stanford's EE261 course. Useful for Fourier intuition and applications; follow with a measure-theoretic treatment for deeper analysis.
books.prerequisites: Calculus, complex numbers and linear algebra.

books.title: Notes on Diffy Qs: Differential Equations for Engineers
books.author: Jiří Lebl
books.note: Introduces ODEs with computation, modeling and examples. A useful first encounter, but its engineering orientation should be supplemented by proof-based analysis.

books.title: Distributions, Elliptic Regularity, and Applications to PDEs
books.author: Semyon Dyatlov
books.note: Develops distributions and elliptic methods through applications including Hodge theory. These graduate notes are a specialized analytic path, not an elementary PDE survey.
books.prerequisites: Real and functional analysis; Fourier analysis.

books.title: Topology Without Tears
books.author: Sidney A. Morris
books.note: A first course emphasizing topological definitions and proof practice. Useful before algebraic topology; elementary prerequisites do not mean the abstractions require little effort.

books.title: Algebraic Topology
books.author: Allen Hatcher
books.note: Geometric examples accompany fundamental groups, homology and cohomology. A substantial first graduate text; 'introductory' refers to the field, not to university mathematics.
books.archiveNote: 2000 archive · noncommercial paper or electronic copies permitted; other rights reserved.

books.title: Categorical Homotopy Theory
books.author: Emily Riehl
books.note: Develops homotopy-theoretic constructions in a categorical setting. A continuation after basic topology and category theory rather than a first topology course.

books.title: What Is Differential Geometry? Curves and Surfaces
books.author: Anton Petrunin and Sergio Zamora Barrera
books.note: A visual, problem-centered approach to classical curves and surfaces. Emphasizes essential techniques; the authors describe its presentation as elementary and 'virtually rigorous'.

books.title: Lectures on Spaces of Nonpositive Curvature
books.author: Werner Ballmann; appendix by Misha Brin
books.note: Develops nonpositive curvature, boundaries at infinity and rank rigidity, with an appendix on geodesic-flow ergodicity. A specialized continuation, not a general first Riemannian geometry textbook.
books.prerequisites: Riemannian geometry; topology; some dynamical systems.

books.title: Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
books.author: Ana Cannas da Silva
books.note: A graduate introduction to symplectic forms, Hamiltonian geometry and reduction. Efficient for readers with manifold foundations; not an elementary introduction to geometry.
books.prerequisites: Smooth manifolds; differential forms; de Rham cohomology.

books.title: Elementary Number Theory: Primes, Congruences, and Secrets
books.author: William Stein
books.note: Connects classical topics with computation, cryptography and elliptic curves. Broader than a minimal congruences course; later chapters benefit from abstract algebra.
books.prerequisites: Proofs; basic algebra, rings and fields.

topics.title: Algebraic Number Theory & Class Field Theory

books.title: Algebraic Number Theory
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: A standard graduate course with proofs. A natural bridge from fields and Galois theory to arithmetic of number fields.

books.title: Class Field Theory
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: A detailed advanced continuation of algebraic number theory. Read after local and global number-field foundations, not immediately after elementary congruences.

books.title: Notes on Analytic Number Theory
books.author: Kiran S. Kedlaya
books.note: A graduate course on primes, analytic methods and sieve ideas. The freely readable HTML format supports selective study; complex analysis is an essential preparation.
books.label: Read full HTML

books.title: Modular Functions and Modular Forms
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: Introduces arithmetic modular forms with a geometric emphasis. A route from complex analysis and algebra toward arithmetic geometry.

books.title: Abelian Varieties
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: An advanced overview of geometry and arithmetic, including finite-field phenomena. Not every deep result is proved in full.

books.title: Combinatorics and Graph Theory
books.author: David Guichard
books.note: A first introduction to counting and graph theory in a freely readable web format. Useful for building discrete proof techniques before specialized combinatorics.
books.label: Read full HTML

books.title: Applied Combinatorics
books.author: Mitchel T. Keller and William T. Trotter
books.note: Combines enumeration, graphs, posets and optimization. The breadth supports several course choices; the linked full HTML is the established 2016 edition.
books.label: Read full HTML

books.title: generatingfunctionology, 2nd edition
books.author: Herbert S. Wilf
books.note: A focused treatment of generating functions and counting. Read after elementary combinatorics; the authorized free edition is the second, not the commercial third.
books.label: Full PDF via author's page

books.title: Graph Theory and Additive Combinatorics: Exploring Structure and Randomness
books.author: Yufei Zhao
books.note: Connects extremal graph theory, pseudorandomness and additive combinatorics. The full author manuscript differs slightly from the published edition; exercises and companion lectures support study.
books.prerequisites: Undergraduate algebra, analysis and linear algebra.

books.title: Introduction to Probability, 2nd edition
books.author: Charles M. Grinstead and J. Laurie Snell
books.note: Examples and exercises develop discrete and continuous probability, with Markov chains and generating functions. Reviewers note broad coverage; graduate measure theory lies beyond its starting point.
books.label: Full book & PDF

books.title: Probability Theory: STAT310/MATH230
books.author: Amir Dembo
books.note: Graduate course notes for measure-theoretic probability. More concise than a first undergraduate textbook; readers should work through proofs rather than rely only on examples.

books.title: Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems
books.author: Gerald Teschl
books.note: Connects rigorous ODE theory to stability, dynamical systems and chaos. A bridge to graduate dynamics; the author permits personal-use downloads, not unrestricted redistribution.

books.title: Lecture Notes on Ergodic Theory
books.author: Omri Sarig
books.note: A measure-theoretic path into ergodic theory. Best after measure and integration; the author warns that the notes have not been proofread and should be used carefully.

linear-algebra.author: Stephen H. Friedberg, Arnold J. Insel and Lawrence E. Spence

linear-algebra.title: Honors in Linear and Abstract Algebra I
linear-algebra.author: Ivan Ip

abstract-algebra.author: David S. Dummit and Richard M. Foote

commutative-algebra.author: M. F. Atiyah and I. G. Macdonald

algebraic-geometry.author: David Mumford

algebraic-geometry.author: William Fulton

calculus.author: David Cohen, Theodore B. Lee and David Sklar

complex-analysis.author: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi
